editorial_note: Canto 11 data remains under full source and translation review. The Sanskrit and English records are draft material tied to the pinned source; phrase coverage and all lexical choices still require chapter-by-chapter verification.
scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for ŚB 11.9.1–11.9.33; the pinned source group 11.9.17–11.9.18.

entries.sanskrit:
नवमे कुररादिभ्यो देहतश् चोपशिक्षितम् ।

श्रुत्वा यदुः कृतार्थोऽभूद् इति कृष्णेन वर्णितम् ॥

कुरराच् छिक्षितम् आह---परिग्रहो हीति । यद् यत् प्रियतमं तस्य तस्य परिग्रहः । तद् विद्वान् परिग्रहो दुःखम् इति विद्वान्सन्, यस् त्व् अकिञ्चनस् त्यक्त-परिग्रहो न तु दरिद्रः॥१॥
word_for_word: from the kurara and the other gurus
the possession of each such thing
entries.literal_english: In the ninth chapter Kṛṣṇa describes what was learned from the kurara and the other gurus and from the body; after hearing this, Yadu became fulfilled. The kurara teaches that whatever is most dear becomes an object of possession. The wise person knows possession to be suffering and, becoming akiñcana, abandons possessiveness; this does not mean that he is merely destitute.

entries.sanskrit: तद् आह---सामिषम् इति ॥२॥
entries.literal_english: He says this with the verse beginning “with flesh.” Other strong birds that had no flesh attacked the kurara that held it; after giving up that flesh, the kurara found happiness.

entries.sanskrit: अर्भक-शिक्षाम् आह---नेति । गेह-पुत्रिणां तद्वतां या भवति चिन्ता, सा च मे नास्ति । आत्मनैव क्रीडा यस्य । आत्मनि रतिः प्रीतिर् यस्य सः ॥३॥
word_for_word: of those who have a home and children
play is with the Self alone
one for whom this is so
entries.literal_english: He introduces the child's lesson with the word “not.” The anxiety that belongs to people who have a home and children is absent in me. One whose play is with the Self alone and whose delight is in the Self is the one being described.

entries.sanskrit: नन्व् अज्ञ-सर्व-ज्ञयोः किं सादृश्यं नैश्चिन्त्यं परम-सुखम् इत्य् आह---द्वाव् इति । विमुग्धोऽज्ञः जडोऽनुद्यमः एवं-भूतो यो बालो यश् च प्रकृतेः परम् ईश्वरं प्राप्तस् तौ द्वौ ॥४॥
word_for_word: of the ignorant and the all-knowing
one who has reached the Lord beyond prakṛti
entries.literal_english: The question is raised: what similarity can there be between the ignorant and the all-knowing? The intended similarity is freedom from anxiety and supreme happiness. The two are the foolish, inactive child and the person who has attained the Lord beyond prakṛti.

entries.sanskrit: कुमार्याः शिक्षितं वक्तुम् आख्यायिकाम् आह---क्वचिद् इत्य्-आदिना । वृणानान् स्व-वरणायागतान् । बन्धुषु पित्रादिषु ॥५॥
word_for_word: who had come for her own selection
entries.literal_english: To state the maiden's lesson, he tells the illustrative story beginning with “once.” The men had come to choose her for themselves, and the relatives means the parents and others.

entries.sanskrit: शङ्खाः शङ्ख-वलयाः । महद् यथा भवति तथा स्वनं चक्रुः ॥६॥
entries.literal_english: The shells are shell bangles. They made a sound as loud as the verse describes.

entries.sanskrit: सा महती बुद्धिमती । तत् स्वयं शाल्य-वहननम् । जुगुप्सितं दरिद्रता-द्योतकम् । एकैकशः क्रमेणैकम् एकं बभञ्ज स्व-कराद् अपसारितवती ॥७॥
entries.literal_english: She was intelligent. The act in question was husking the rice herself; this was shameful because it revealed poverty. She broke the bangles one by one, successively removing each from her hands.

entries.sanskrit: निरभिदत् पृथक् कृतवती ॥८॥
entries.literal_english: The word nirabhidat means that she separated them, making them distinct from one another.

entries.sanskrit: ननु कुमार्यास् तव च कथं सङ्गतिः ? तत्राह---लोकान् इति ॥९॥
entries.literal_english: One may ask, “What connection is there between the maiden and you?” He answers this by saying that he learned while wandering through the worlds.

entries.sanskrit: वास इति प्रथमान्त-पाठे कलह-हेतुः । वार्ता गोष्ठी हेतुर् भवेद् इत्य् अर्थः॥१०॥
word_for_word: in the reading ending in the nominative
is a cause of a gathering
entries.literal_english: In the reading vāsa, with the nominative ending, residence is a cause of quarrel. Vārtā, conversation or talk, becomes a cause of a gathering. Thus the two readings explain the two forms of social disturbance described in the verse.

entries.sanskrit:
चित्तैकाग्रता द्वैतास्फूर्ति-लक्षण-समाधि-हेतुर् इति शर-काराच् छिक्षितम् इत्य् आह---मन इति । तत्रोपायम् आह---जितेति । आसन-जये श्वास-जयः । तस्य च जये श्वासाधीनं मनो निश्चलं भवति ।

ननु क्षणं निश्चलं सद् अपि मनो विषय-वासनया यदि विक्षिप्येत सुषुप्ताव् इव सर्वथा लीयेत वा तदा किं ? तत्राह---वैराग्येति । वैराग्येणाविक्षिप्यमाणम् अभ्यास-योगेन लक्ष्ये ध्रियमाणं स्थिरी-क्रियमाणम् ॥११॥
word_for_word: the cause of samādhi marked by the non-appearance of duality
one who has mastered the posture
the mind dependent on the breath
entries.literal_english: One-pointedness of mind is the cause of samādhi, whose mark is the absence of the appearance of duality; this is learned from the arrow-maker. The method is mastery of posture and breath. When breath is mastered, the mind that depends on it becomes steady. But even a briefly steady mind may be disturbed by impressions of sense objects, or may dissolve completely as in deep sleep. The answer is dispassion: by dispassion it is not distracted, and by the yoga of practice it is held on the goal and made firm.

entries.sanskrit:
एकत्रेति कुत्र ? तद् आह---यस्मिन्न् इति यल् लय-विक्षेपात्मकं मनः, एतद् यस्मिन् परमानन्द-रूपे भगवति लब्धास्पदं सत् कर्म-रेणून् कर्म-वासना मुञ्चति तस्मिन् ।

ननु कर्म-वासना-त्यागेऽपि सुषुप्ति-वल्लयो दुर्वारः ? न, सत्त्वेनेति । वृद्धेनोपशमात्मकेन रजस्-तमसोर् अभावे विक्षेप-लयाभावान् निर्वाणम् अवृत्तिकं ध्येयाकारेणावस्थानम् उपैति । कुतः ? अनिन्धनम् । इन्धनं गुणास् तत्-कार्यं च, तद्-रहितम् । तद् उक्तं योग-शास्त्रे,

> मनसो वृत्ति-शून्यस्य ब्रह्माकारतया स्थितिः । >
> यासंप्रज्ञात-नामासौ समाधिर् अभिधीयते ॥ इति ।
word_for_word: the mind characterized by dissolution and distraction
in Bhagavān whose form is supreme bliss
when rajas and tamas are absent
because distraction and dissolution are absent
remaining in the form of the meditation object
entries.literal_english: Where is the mind fixed in one place? It is fixed in Bhagavān, whose form is supreme bliss. The mind, characterized by dissolution and distraction, finds its seat there and releases the particles of karma, namely the karmic tendencies. Even after abandoning those tendencies, might dissolution like sleep remain unavoidable? No: when sattva has developed into pacification and rajas and tamas are absent, distraction and dissolution cease. It attains nirvāṇa, a state without mental modifications, remaining in the form of the meditation object. This is without fuel, because the fuel is the guṇas and their effects, which are absent. The cited yoga teaching calls this the mind without modifications abiding in the form of Brahman, known as non-conceptual samādhi.

entries.sanskrit: ततश् च न द्वैत-स्फूर्तिर् इत्य् आह---तदेति । बहिर् दर्शनादिना । अन्तरं स्मृत्या । इषौ गतात्मा तस्य ऋजू-करणे दत्त-चित्तो भेरी-घोषैर् अन्तिके व्रजन्तं नृपतिम् अपि न वेद तद्वत् ॥१३॥
word_for_word: there is no appearance of duality
externally, through seeing and the like
with the self or mind entered into the arrow
giving his attention to making it straight
entries.literal_english: Then the appearance of duality is absent: externally there is no awareness through seeing and the like, and internally there is no awareness through memory. The arrow-maker, whose mind had entered the arrow and was intent on straightening it, did not even know the king passing nearby amid the sound of drums. The sage should be likewise absorbed.

entries.sanskrit: सर्पाच् छिक्षितम् आह---एक-चारीति । योगि-संमर्दस्यापि त्यागे कुमारी गुरुः, जन-सङ्ग-त्यागे सर्पः । स यथा जनाच् छङ्कमान एकाकी विचरति नियत-निकेत-रहितश् च सदाप्रमत्तश् चैकान्तवासी च । आचारैर् गतिभिः सविषो निर्विषो वेति न लक्ष्यते च । असहायश् च मित-भाषी च तद्वन् मुनिर् वर्तेतेत्य् अर्थः ॥१४॥
word_for_word: in abandoning even the crowd of yogis
entries.literal_english: The snake teaches solitary conduct. The maiden teaches the abandonment of a crowd even of yogis, while the snake teaches abandonment of people's association. As a snake, wary of people, wanders alone without a fixed dwelling, remains constantly vigilant and lives in solitude, and its venomous or non-venomous nature is not known from its conduct or movements, so the sage should live without assistance and speak little.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, गृहारम्भ इति । अध्रुवात्मनो नश्वर-देहस्य । सुखं यथा भवति तथा वर्धते ॥१५॥
word_for_word: for one whose nature is impermanent
entries.literal_english: Moreover, the phrase about undertaking a house concerns the impermanent, perishable body. The snake, entering a residence made by another, increases its happiness as appropriate; the sage should not waste effort constructing a house for a body that will not last.

entries.sanskrit: कारक-सामग्री-निरपेक्षात् केवलाद् ईश्वराद् विश्व-सृष्टि-संहाराव् ऊर्ण-नाभि-दृष्टान्तेन मया संभाविताव् इति वक्तुं प्रथमं संहार-प्रकारम् आह---एक इति सार्ध-त्रयेण । एकः कारक-निरपेक्षः । पूर्व-सृष्टम् इदं जगत् काल-कलया काल-शक्त्या संहृत्य एक एवाद्वितीयः सजातीय-विजातीय-भेद-शून्योऽभूत् ॥१६॥
word_for_word: independent of the collection of causal instruments
the creation and dissolution of the universe
through the example of the spider
became alone and without a second
entries.literal_english: Through the spider example I have understood that the Lord alone, independent of any collection of causal instruments, performs the creation and dissolution of the universe. First the manner of dissolution is stated: the one Lord, independent of causal instruments, withdrew this previously created universe by the power of Time and became alone, without a second.

entries.sanskrit: कारण-भूतासु सत्त्वादिषु शक्तिष्व् अपि साम्यं नीतासु सतीषु । गुण-साम्यं प्रधानं तद्-उपाधिः पुरुषश् च तयोर् ईश्वरः । परावराणां परे ब्रह्मादयः, अवरेऽन्ये च मुक्ता जीवाः, तेषां परमः प्राप्य आस्ते। कुतः ? कैवल्य-संज्ञितो मोक्ष-शब्दाभिधेयः । तत्र हेतुः---केवलेति । केवलो निर्विषयः स्व-प्रकाशः आनन्दानांसन्दोहः समूहः परमानन्द इत्य् अर्थः । कुतः ? निरुपाधिकः ॥१७-१८॥
word_for_word: in the powers that are causes
the higher, Brahmā and the others
the lower, the other liberated beings
remains as the one to be attained
entries.literal_english: When the causal powers beginning with sattva are brought to equilibrium, the equilibrium of the guṇas is called Pradhāna, Puruṣa is its limiting adjunct, and their Lord is Īśvara. He remains as the supreme object to be attained by the higher—Brahmā and the others—and by the lower, the other liberated beings. He is called Kaivalya, the name of liberation. Kaivalya is without an object, self-luminous, a mass of bliss, and without limiting adjuncts.

entries.sanskrit: अतः केवलाद् एव सृष्टिं दर्शयति---केवलेनात्मानुभावेन कालेन । सूत्रं क्रिया-शक्ति-प्रधानं महत्-तत्त्वं सृजति । जीव-संसार-हेतु-भूते सूत्रे सृष्टेऽपि त्वं मा भैर् इति संबोधयति । अरिन्दम अरीन् रागादीन् दमयितुं समर्थ ॥१९॥
word_for_word: by Time in the form of His own independent power
which is the cause of the living beings' transmigration
entries.literal_english: Therefore creation is also shown as proceeding from the Lord alone, through Time in the form of His own power. He creates the Sūtra, the principle of mahat and chiefly the power of action. Although this Sūtra has been created as the cause of the living beings' transmigration, the address “O subduer of enemies” reassures Arindama: he is capable of subduing enemies such as attachment.

entries.sanskrit: सूत्रस्यैव व्यक्ति-शब्देनोच्यमानस्य ताम् इति स्त्री-लिङ्गेन परामर्शः । त्रि-गुण-व्यक्तिं गुण-त्रय-कार्यम् । अत एव विश्वतो-मुखं नाना-विधं त्रि-गुणात्मकं विश्वम् अहङ्कार-द्वारेण सृजन्तीम् । त्रि-गुण-कार्यस्य सूत्र-संज्ञायां कारणम् आह---यस्मिन्न् इति । कारण-भूते समष्टि-रूपे यस्मिन्न् इदं विश्वं प्रोतं ग्रथितम्, वायुर् वै गौतम, सूत्रं वायुना वै गौतम, सूत्रेणायं च लोकः परश् च लोकः सर्वाणि च भूतानि सन्दृब्धानि [बृ।आ।उ। ३.७.२] इति श्रुतेः । येन वाय्व्-आत्मना प्राण-रूपेण जीवः संसरति ॥२०॥
word_for_word: of the Sūtra itself, spoken of by the word manifestation
it is referred to in the feminine gender
the manifestation of the three guṇas
the effect of the three guṇas
the manifold universe made of the three guṇas
in which this universe is woven
O Gautama, it is the Sūtra by air
सूत्रेण अयम् लोकः परः लोकः सर्वाणि भूतानि
by the Sūtra this world, the next world, and all beings
by which, in the form of air and vital breath
entries.literal_english: The Sūtra is itself being referred to by the feminine word “that.” It is the manifestation of the three guṇas and the effect of their threefold activity. Through ahaṅkāra it creates the many-sided universe made of the three guṇas. The reason it is called Sūtra is that, in its causal aggregate form, this universe is woven in it. The cited Śruti says that air is the Sūtra, and that by the Sūtra this world, the next world, and all beings are strung together. Through it, in the form of air and vital breath, the living being transmigrates.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं शिक्षितम् अर्थम् उक्त्वा दृष्टान्तम् आह---यथेति । हृदयाद् उद्गताम् । वक्त्रतो वक्त्रेण सन्तत्य प्रसार्य विहृत्य क्रीडित्वा ॥२१॥
word_for_word: having stated the meaning learned in this way
from the mouth, by the mouth
entries.literal_english: Having stated the meaning learned in this way, he gives the example of the spider. Its web has arisen from its heart; it extends it continuously from its mouth, sports with it and plays.

entries.sanskrit: भगवद्-ध्यान-पराणां तत्-सारूप्यं न चित्रम् इति पेशस्कृतो भ्रमर-विशेषाज् ज्ञातम् इत्य् आह---यत्र यत्रेति । सकलम् एकाग्रम् ॥२२॥
word_for_word: for those devoted to meditation on Bhagavān
a particular kind of bee or wasp
entries.literal_english: It is not strange that those devoted to meditation on Bhagavān attain similarity to Him; this is known from the peśaskṛt, a particular bee or wasp. Wherever the mind is placed, the whole of it should be one-pointed.

entries.sanskrit: कुड्यां प्रवेशितो निरुद्धो भयेन ध्यायन् सात्मतां तत् सारूप्यम् । साम्यताम् इति पाठे त्व् आर्षता । पूर्व-रूपम् असन्त्यजन्न् इत्य् अस्यायम् अभिप्रायः । यदा तेनैव देहेनान्य-सारूप्यं दृश्यते तदा किं वक्तव्यं देहान्तरेण सारूप्यं घटत् इति ॥२३॥
word_for_word: likeness through another body takes place
entries.literal_english: The insect, confined in a wall and meditating on the wasp through fear, attains its likeness. In the reading sāmya­tām there is an archaic form. The phrase “without abandoning its former form” addresses the question: if likeness to another is seen with that same body, what should be said when likeness arises through another body?

entries.sanskrit: स्व-देहाद् एव शिक्षितम् आह---स्वात्मेति । स्वात्मनो देहाच् छिक्षिताम् ॥२४॥
word_for_word: from the body belonging to oneself
entries.literal_english: He says that the lesson was learned from his own body—from the body belonging to himself.

entries.sanskrit: गुरुत्वे हेतुः--विरक्ति-विवेकयोर् हेतुः । विरक्ति-हेतुत्वम् आह---सत्त्व-निधनम् उत्पत्ति-विनाशौ बिभ्रत् स्म । किं च, सततं सन्ततम् आर्त्य्-उदर्कं दुःस्वम् एवोत्तर-फलं बिभ्रत् । यद् वा, सततार्तिर् एवोदर्क उत्तर-फलं यस्य तत् सत्त्व-निधनं बिभ्रत्। विवेक-हेतुत्वम् आह---तत्त्वानि इति । यथा यथावत् । एवम् अत्युपकारित्वेऽपि देहेनैवास्था कर्तव्येत्य् आह---तथापि इति । पारक्यं श्व-शृगालादि-भक्ष्यम् इति निश्चितवान् ॥२५॥
word_for_word: the reason for its being a guru
the cause of detachment and discrimination
the ending or death of the embodied being
having suffering as its later result
only suffering as the final fruit
food for dogs, jackals and the like
entries.literal_english: The body is a guru because it causes detachment and discrimination. It causes detachment because it undergoes birth and death and constantly bears suffering as its final result. It causes discrimination because through it one understands the fundamental principles as they are. Yet, despite this usefulness, he has determined that the body belongs to others—it is food for dogs, jackals and the like.

entries.sanskrit: सततार्त्य्-उदर्कतां प्रपञ्चयति---जायेति द्वाभ्याम् । यस्य देहस्य प्रिय-चिकीर्षया भोग-संपादनेच्छया जायादि-वर्गान् वितन्वन् पुष्णाति पुरुषः । कथं-भूतः ? स-कृच्छ्रं यथा भवति तथावरुद्धानि सञ्चितानि धनानि येन सः, देह-विशेषणं वा । स देहः स्वान्ते स्वस्यायुषोऽन्तेऽवसीदति नश्यति । किं च, देह-नाशेऽपि न दुःख-समाप्तिर् इत्य् आह---अस्य पुरुषस्य देहान्तर-बीजं कर्म सृष्ट्वेति । वृक्षस्येव धर्मो यस्य सः ॥२६॥
word_for_word: the condition whose final result is continual suffering
with the desire to obtain enjoyment
at the end of its lifespan
even when the body is destroyed
there is no end of suffering
karma is the seed of another body
having the nature of a tree
entries.literal_english: He elaborates the body's continual suffering through the two verses beginning with the wife. A person, wishing to please this body and obtain enjoyment, expands and maintains a wife and other dependants, using wealth accumulated with great difficulty. That body sinks and perishes at the end of its lifespan. Even when it is destroyed, suffering does not end, because karma has been created as the seed of another body, whose process is like that of a tree leaving a seed.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, जिह्वेति । अमुं देहं तद् अभिमानिनं पुरुषं वा एकतो रसं प्रति जिह्वा अपकर्षत्य् आच्छिनत्ति । कर्हि कदाचित् तर्षा पिपासा जलं प्रति । शिश्नो व्यवायं प्रति । त्वक् स्पर्शं प्रति । उदरम् अन्न-मात्रं प्रति । श्रवणं शब्दं प्रति । घ्राणो गन्धं प्रति । चपल-दृक् रूपं प्रति । क्व च क्वचित् स्व-स्व-विषयं प्रति कर्म-शक्तिः । अन्यद् अपि कर्मेन्द्रियम् । लुनन्ति त्रोटयन्ति ॥२७॥
word_for_word: or the person who identifies with it
the organ of generation toward intercourse
each power of action toward its own object
entries.literal_english: The tongue drags this body—or the person who identifies with it—toward taste. At times thirst pulls it toward water; the generative organ toward intercourse; the skin toward touch; the stomach toward food; the ear toward sound; the nose toward smell; and the restless eye toward form. Each organ of action pulls toward its own object. In this way the senses cut and tear the person apart.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं देहो गुरुर् इत्य्-आदि त्रिभिर् विरक्ति-विवेक-हेतुत्वम् उपपाद्येदानीम् अस्य देहस्यातिदुर्लभत्वं दर्शयन्न् ईश्वर-निष्ठां विधत्ते---सृष्ट्वेति द्वाभ्याम् । पुराणि शरीराणि । पुरुषं पुरुष-देहम् । ब्रह्मणोऽवलोकायापरोक्ष्याय धिषणा बुद्धिर् यस्मिंस् तम् । तद् उक्तम्---तासां मे पौरुषी प्रिया इति । श्रुतिश् च---पुरुषत्वे चाविस्तराम् आत्मा इत्य्-आदि । [ईश्वरो हि करणाधिष्ठात्रीर् अग्न्यादि-देवता वाग्-आदिभिः सह सृष्टवान् । ताश् च तं प्रति भोगार्थं शरीरम् अयाचन्त । स च ताभ्यो गो-शरीरम् आश्व-शरीरं पुरुष-शरीरं यथाक्रमम् आनीतवान् । ततस् ता देवताः सोऽब्रवीद् यथायतनं चक्षुर्-आदि-स्थानम् अस्मिन् देहे प्रविशतेति । तद् आह---ताभ्य इत्य्-आदि ।] तथा---ताभ्यो गामानयत्ता अब्रुवन् न वैनोऽयम् अलम् इति ताभ्योऽश्वमानयत्ता अब्रुवन् न वैनोऽयम् अलम् इति ताभ्यः पुरुषमानयत्ता अब्रुवन् सुकृतं बत इति च ॥२८॥
word_for_word: through the three verses beginning “the body is a guru”
its being a cause of detachment and discrimination
the extreme rarity of this body
he establishes devotion to the Lord
with the two verses beginning “having created”
the human being, the human body
among these, the human form is dear to Me
the deities presiding over the organs, beginning with fire
together with speech and the other faculties
they requested a body for enjoyment
a cow body, a horse body, and a human body
their respective places beginning with the eye
entries.literal_english: Having established through the three preceding verses that the body causes detachment and discrimination, he now shows its extreme rarity and establishes devotion to the Lord. The two verses beginning “having created” distinguish the many bodies from the human body, whose intelligence is capable of directly seeing Brahman. The source then includes an extended account: the Lord created the deities presiding over the organs, beginning with fire, together with speech and the other faculties. They requested bodies for enjoyment, but rejected the cow and horse bodies as insufficient and praised the human body as excellent; they were then told to enter their respective places, beginning with the eye. The source itself marks the attached note as probably interpolated.

entries.sanskrit: तस्माद् बहूनां सम्भवानां जन्मनाम् अन्तेमानुष्यम् अनित्यम् अप्य् अर्थदं पुरुषार्थ-प्रापकं दैवाल् लब्ध्वेदम् अनुमृत्यु अन्व् अनु निरन्तरं मृत्यवो यस्य, तद् यावन् न पतेत् तावद् एव तूर्णं शीघ्रं निःश्रेयसाय यतेत । विषयः पुनः सर्वतः पश्व्-आदि-योनिष्व् अपि स्याद् एव ॥२९॥
word_for_word: at the end of many births
impermanent yet giving the highest purpose
one should strive for the highest good
even in animal and other births
entries.literal_english: Therefore, after many births, one obtains human birth. Although impermanent, it gives the highest purpose and enables the human goal. Since death follows it continually, one should strive immediately for the highest good, before the body falls. Sense objects, however, are available everywhere, even in animal and other forms of life.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं हेयोपादेय-विवेकं बहुधा निरूप्येदानीं यद् उक्तं, त्वं तु कल्पः कविर् दक्षः [भा।पु। ११.७.२८] इत्य्-आदि तत्रोत्तरम् आह---एवम् इति । एवं बहुभ्यो गुरुभ्यः शिक्षितेन विशिष्टं ज्ञानम् एवालोकः प्रदीपो यस्य सः । सप्तम्य् अन्तं वा आत्म-विशेषणम् । आत्मनि स्थित एव महीं विचरामि ।
word_for_word: discrimination between what is to be rejected and accepted
entries.literal_english: Having explained discrimination between what is to be rejected and accepted in many ways, he answers that the distinctive knowledge learned from many gurus is his light and lamp. He wanders the earth abiding in the Self.

entries.sanskrit: ननु किं बहुभिर् गुरुभिः ? न हि श्वेतकेतु-भृगु-प्रमुखैर् बहवो गुरव आश्रिताः । तत्राह---न ह्य् एकस्माद् इति । बहुधा स-प्रपञ्च-निष्प्रपञ्च-भेदादिभिः । अयं भावः---नैते परमार्थोपदेश-गुरवः, किन्त्व् अन्वय-व्यतिरेकाभ्याम् आत्मन्य् असम्भावनादि-मात्र-निवर्तकाः, तेषां बहुत्वं युक्तम् एवेति । ज्ञान-प्रदं गुरुम् एकम् एव वक्ष्यति, मद्-अभिज्ञं गुरुं शान्तम् उपासीत [भा।पु। ११.१०.५] इति । उक्तं च, तस्माद् गुरुं प्रपद्येत जिज्ञासुः श्रेय उत्तमं [भा।पु। ११.३.२२] इति ॥३१॥
word_for_word: with Śvetaketu, Bhṛgu and others as examples
through distinctions such as with manifestation and without manifestation
these are not gurus of ultimate instruction
through agreement and difference or absence
doubt and the like concerning the Self
one should worship the peaceful one
entries.literal_english: One may ask why many gurus are needed, since figures such as Śvetaketu and Bhṛgu did not rely on many. The answer is that these are not gurus of the ultimate instruction. They merely remove doubts about the Self through reasoning by agreement and difference; for that purpose their plurality is appropriate. A single guru who gives knowledge, knows Me and is peaceful will be stated later, and the seeker of the highest good should worship such a guru.

entries.sanskrit: विप्रो दत्तात्रेयः, योग-र्द्धिम् आपुर् उभयीं यद् उहैहयाद्याः इत्य् उक्तत्वात् । यथागतं तथैव । यदृच्छया ययाव् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३२॥
entries.literal_english: The brāhmaṇa was Dattātreya. Yadu, the Haihayas and others attained the twofold yogic perfection, as has been stated. He departed just as he had come, going wherever he pleased.

entries.sanskrit:
भगवान् स्वीयं ब्रह्म-वित् कुलम् इति श्लाघते, नः पूर्वेषां पूर्व-ज इति । अत्र सङ्ग्रह-श्लोकाः---

> कपोत-मीन-हरिण- कुमारी-गज-पन्न-गाः । >
> पतङ्गः कुररश् चाष्टौ हेयार्थे गुरवो मताः ॥ >
> मधु-कृन् मधु-हर्ता च पिङ्गलाथ द्वयोस् त्रयः । >
> उपादेयार्थ-विज्ञाने शेषाः पृथ्व्य्-आदयो मताः ॥ >
> तद् अवान्तर-मेदश् च तत्र तत्र स्फुटी-कृतः । >
> अध्याय-त्रितये चाष्ट- नवाष्टाव् ईरिताः क्रमात् ॥३३॥
word_for_word: His own lineage of knowers of Brahman
pigeon, fish, deer, maiden, elephant and snake
gurus concerning what is to be rejected
the bee, the honey-thief and Piṅgalā
in knowledge of what is to be adopted
the remaining gurus, beginning with earth
made explicit in their respective places
eight, nine and eight in sequence
entries.literal_english: The Lord praises His own lineage of knowers of Brahman, saying that the teacher is the ancestor of the ancestors. The closing summary verses classify the gurus: pigeon, fish, deer, maiden, elephant, snake, moth and kurara are teachers concerning what should be rejected; the bee, the honey-thief and Piṅgalā concern what should be adopted; the remaining gurus beginning with earth are also included. Their subdivisions are made clear in their respective places, and the three chapters speak of them in counts of eight, nine and eight.
